(b) Toolbar customization mechanism (`initToolbarCustomization`, 11149-11233): storage key `'nemo-timeline-toolbar-hidden'` (`KEY`), JSON shape a flat array of hidden button-id strings (e.g. `["btn-tween-curves","btn-shadow-guides"]`), read via `readHidden()` (`JSON.parse(localStorage.getItem(KEY)||'[]')`, try/caught to `[]`). `candidates()` selects `:scope > button.tb[id]` under `#tl-toolbar`, filtered to exclude the trigger itself (`b!==trigger`) AND any id in `ALWAYS_VISIBLE=['btn-ff','btn-pf','btn-play','btn-nf','btn-lf','btn-loop']` — the transport cluster, excluded by explicit design comment (11151-11157, quoting 2026-07-27 feedback: 'tout ça ne doit pas y apparaître, il reste quoi qu'il arrive') rather than shown disabled. `apply()` (11169-11178) first drops any stored id that has since become protected (a stale localStorage entry from before `ALWAYS_VISIBLE` existed, or hand-edited), persisting the cleaned list back if it changed; it then force-removes `toolbar-user-hidden` from every `ALWAYS_VISIBLE` button and toggles that same class on each `candidates()` button per the (cleaned) hidden list. The class itself is CSS-driven: `#tl-toolbar .toolbar-user-hidden{display:none!important;}` (style.css:913) — `apply()` never touches inline style or `display` directly. The overflow trigger (`#btn-toolbar-customize`) is never a member of `candidates()` (excluded by the `b!==trigger` filter), so it can never receive the hidden class and is never hideable — matching the lead-in comment's own claim (11147-11148: 'the overflow button is intentionally never hideable, so hidden controls always remain recoverable').

(c) The three localStorage keys touched anywhere in this span, each owned by tweens.js's own read/write functions but exercised here via `initOnionTintShift` (11366-11386): `nemo-onion-tint-prev`/`nemo-onion-tint-next` — written by `setOnionTint('prev'|'next',hex)` (tweens.js:4601-4604) on every `tp`/`tn` `input` event (11373-11374); REMOVED (both, together) by `localStorage.removeItem(...)` inside the `tr` (reset) click handler (11375-11378), which then calls `sync()`+`renderOS()`+`SMEngineBridge.renderNow()` — the only removal point for either tint key anywhere in this scope. `nemo-onion-shift` — written (never removed) by `setOnionShift({x,y,next})` (tweens.js:4616-4619) from `pushShift()` (11383), itself called on every `sx`/`sy`/`sn` input/change (11384) AND from the `sr` (shift-reset) click handler (11385), which zeroes `sx.value`/`sy.value` in the DOM first and then calls `pushShift()` — so a 'reset' of shift is a normal write of `{x:0,y:0,next:sn.checked}`, not a key removal, unlike the tint reset.

(d) `state.revisionView`'s value cycles `all`→`mine`→`revisions`→`all` via `REVISION_VIEW_ORDER.indexOf`+modulo (11244-11246) on every `#btn-revision-view` click; the button's own label is re-set from `REVISION_VIEW_LABELS` (`{all:'Tout',mine:'Mes traits',revisions:'Corrections'}`, hard-coded French, not routed through `SM.t`/i18n.js) and its `active` class toggled when not `'all'` (11247-11248); the sole side effect is `window.SMEngineBridge.renderNow()` (11248) — no `saveActiveLayerFrame`/`pushUndoLayers`/document mutation call appears anywhere in the handler, confirmed by direct read and by grep restricted to this handler's own four lines. Its single render-side reader is engine-bridge.js's `buildSceneJson`, at two sites: the per-item scene-build loop (engine-bridge.js:1331 `'mine'` branch, 1333 `'revisions'` branch) and a second, explicitly-commented-redundant `'mine'` filter later in the same function (engine-bridge.js:3411, 'filtered out of the scene above anyway, but be explicit') — both are pure read-time filters over which review/correction ghosts are included in the built scene JSON, confirming the lead-in comment's own claim (11238-11239: 'purely a render-time filter ... never touches the document') by direct grep of `revisionView` across `engine-bridge.js` (three hits, all reads) and across `app.js`/`tweens.js` (zero hits).

(e) Onion subsystem seams: `setOnionSpan(prev,next)` (11264-11280) sets `window._omSpan` to `{prev:9999,next:9999}` when `prev<0` (the 'all' preset) or `{prev,next}` otherwise; computes `inF=prev<0?0:Math.max(0,cf-prev)` and `outF=prev<0?state.totalFrames-1:Math.min(state.totalFrames-1,cf+next)`; writes the two marker DOM elements' `dataset.frame`; calls `window.SM.setOnionRange(inF,outF)` (timeline.js:846, sets `state.onionIn`/`state.onionOut` then `renderOS()` — bodies out of THIS leaf's own scope, cited by line only) with `-1` on either argument having no special meaning to `setOnionRange` itself (the `-1`→`9999`/`0`/`totalFrames-1` translation happens entirely inside `setOnionSpan`, before the call); then calls `window.updateOmMarkers(cf,state.totalFrames)`. `setOnionSpan` is called exactly four times in this scope, all from the four `om-span-*` click handlers (11281-11284) — `setOnionSpan(1,1)`/`(2,2)`/`(5,5)`/`(-1,-1)` — with no other internal or external caller found by a whole-`src` grep restricted to `setOnionSpan(`. `window._omFollow`/`window.updateOmMarkers` are owned by ui.js (ui.js:1041-1058, cited by line only, not redefined here) — this scope only reads/writes `_omFollow` (11287, 11289) and calls `updateOmMarkers` (11280, 11291). `initOnionPopover` (11298-11322): right-click (`contextmenu`, preventDefault+stopPropagation) on `#btn-os` positions and shows `#onion-pop` (`display='block'`, clamped horizontally to the viewport and placed ABOVE the button since the timeline sits at the window's bottom, measured post-`display:block` so `offsetHeight` is real); a document-level `pointerdown` listener hides it on any outside click; left-click on the SAME `#btn-os` is wired separately, OUTSIDE this IIFE, at line 11145 (prior leaf, out of THIS scope) and keeps toggling on/off as before. The popover re-hosts the right-panel's own Onion Skin section header (`#onion-sec .phdr`, 11317) as an identical `SM.toggleOnion()` trigger, and syncs the `#os-st-panel` badge's text/color from `state.onionSkin` once at init (11318-11320) — the badge itself is otherwise updated by `toggleOnion` (timeline.js:459, out of scope). `initOnionTintShift`'s `sync()` (11370-11373) prefills `tp.value`/`tn.value` from `onionTint('prev'|'next')` (tweens.js:4597, reads the localStorage key or `ONION_TINT_DEFAULTS`) and `sx.value`/`sy.value`/`sn.checked` from `onionShift()` (tweens.js:4608, reads `nemo-onion-shift` or `{x:0,y:0,next:false}`); it is called once at IIFE-init (11386) AND again on every `#btn-os` `contextmenu` (11384-11385, via `setTimeout(sync,0)`) — the lead-in comment (11362-11365) states both call points explicitly ('pré-remplis à l'ouverture du popover ET au chargement'). `setOnionShift`'s payload is always the full `{x,y,next}` object, never a partial patch (tweens.js:4616-4619 JSON-stringifies exactly those three keys with `Number(...)||0`/`!!` coercion).

(f) `initCompPreview` (11323-11332) and `initLipSync` (11333-11360): `initCompPreview` reads nothing from the active layer itself — `#btn-comp-preview` click calls `SMCompPreview.toggle()` (guarded `window.SMCompPreview`) and `#comp-frame-strip` dblclick calls `SMCompPreview.show()` (guarded), both no-argument calls into a module out of scope. `initLipSync`'s own `ld()` helper (11334) is the symbolId gate: it returns `state.layers[state.activeLayerIdx]` only when that layer has BOTH a truthy `.symbolId` AND `window.SMLipSync` is present, else `null` — every settings-field handler and the apply button all early-return through this same gate. The four numeric fields (`lip-start`/`lip-end`/`lip-sens`/`lip-hold`) write onto `SMLipSync.settingsOf(l)` (lipsync.js:45, cited by line only) with local clamps: `start`/`end` floored at 0, `sensitivity` floored at 0.2, `hold` floored at 1. `lip-track` writes `settingsOf(l).trackIdx` from `parseInt(sel.value)||0`. `#btn-lip-apply` calls `SMLipSync.analyze(l)` (lipsync.js:149, cited by line only) with no options argument; on `res.error` it shows a `SM.t('lipNoAudio')` toast and returns without writing anything; otherwise it calls `saveAllLayerFrames()`+`pushUndoLayers(true)` (persistence/undo BEFORE the write), then `SMLipSync.apply(state.activeLayerIdx,res)` (lipsync.js:177, cited by line only, layer index + analysis result, no options argument here either) whose own return value's `.written` count is interpolated into the success toast; finally `loadFrame(state.currentFrame)`+`updateUI()`+`SMEngineBridge.renderNow()` refresh the view. Neither `analyze` nor `apply`'s own bodies are reproduced — both are lipsync.js's own module, out of scope.

(g) The `#tl-cf` clamp rule (11401-11411): `var v=Math.max(1,Math.min(state.totalFrames,parseInt(this.value)||1));this.value=v;` clamps the typed/scrubbed 1-based frame number into `[1,state.totalFrames]` and writes the clamped value BACK into the input, THEN (if playing) calls `stopPlay()` and calls `goToFrame(v-1)` (0-based). The lead-in comment (11396-11400) explains why the clamp must happen here rather than being left to `goToFrame` itself: `goToFrame` (app.js:5112-5113) reads `if(idx<0||idx>=state.totalFrames)return;` — an out-of-range index is a silent no-op, not a clamp, so a drag-past-the-end without a local clamp would leave the `#tl-cf` input showing a stale/invalid number that nothing ever applied to the actual frame.
